_: Parameter sets for the parity corpus, as PARTIAL TraceParamsInput trees.
Partial on purpose: both halves run the same engine/params.ts sanitizeTraceParams() over the same
literal, so every field this file leaves out is filled from the engine's own defaults on both
sides. Writing out all thirty-two knobs here would freeze a copy of those defaults in a file that
nothing updates, and the day the vendored engine changes one, this corpus would be testing a
parameter set the product no longer ships.
THE TRAP THIS FILE SITS ON. Every enum below is a plain string, and sanitizeTraceParams's enumOf
helper answers an unrecognised string with the documented DEFAULT rather than throwing — so
'OUTLNE' would silently trace centreline and the corpus would quietly stop covering outline mode.
e2e/trace-parity-unit.spec.ts asserts the sanitised tree really came out as written, which is the
only thing that keeps a typo here loud.
Keys are the second half of a caseId: <fixture>/<params>.
What the product actually ships. sanitizeTraceParams({}) is defaultTraceParams(): CENTERLINE
vector mode and AutoMode.SUGGEST, so this case runs the classifier (engine/classify.ts, Math.log
and Math.atan2), the thinner and the skeleton tracer. It is the widest parity surface in the
corpus and the one a designer's trace actually takes.
The existing oracle's parameters, copied from e2e/trace-engine-unit.spec.ts's outlineParams():
OUTLINE rather than CENTERLINE so a filled shape traces its boundary and not its skeleton, and
auto detection OFF so the note list is a function of the trace rather than of the classifier.
Reusing them rather than inventing a set means the disc cases here and the geometry assertions
there are talking about the same run.
